subject: Banking
title: Credit Utilization Secrets
description: A fast breakdown of Credit Utilization Secrets for builders.

hook.text: Using more than 30% of your credit limit hurts your score. But the optimal utilization rate is actually below 10%.

buildup.text: Credit utilization is the second biggest factor: 30% of your FICO score.

discovery.text: People with 800+ scores typically use only 7% of their available credit. Low utilization signals financial discipline.

twist.text: Utilization resets monthly. A high balance one month can tank your score.

climax.text: Utilization is the fastest lever for your score. Unlike payment history.

punchline.text: Stay under 10%. Utilization is the fastest way to change your credit score.

quiz.question: What credit utilization do people with 800+ scores typically have?

details.summary: Credit utilization, the percentage of available credit you are using, is the second most important factor in your FICO score. Keeping utilization below 30 percent helps your score, but below 10 percent is optimal.
details.whyItMatters: Utilization is the fastest way to change your credit score because it updates every billing cycle. Understanding utilization mechanics lets you strategically time payments and credit limit requests to maximize your score.
takeaways: Utilization below 10 percent produces the highest credit scores
Both overall and per-card utilization ratios affect your score
Paying before the statement date can lower reported utilization

faq.question: Does closing a credit card hurt utilization?
faq.answer: Yes. Closing a card reduces your total available credit while your balances stay the same, increasing your utilization ratio. Keep old cards open with small occasional purchases to maintain a higher total credit limit.

faq.question: When is utilization reported to credit bureaus?
faq.answer: Most issuers report your balance on your statement closing date, not your payment due date. Paying down your balance before the statement closes results in a lower reported utilization, regardless of how much you actually spend monthly.
